Pala Empire.fact: At its zenith under emperors Dharmapala and Devapala in the early ninth century, the Pala empire was the dominant power in the northern Indian subcontinent, with its territory stretching across the Gangetic plain down to the Vindya range and may have extended to Goalpara in Assam. Persian art.fact: The tombs were looted following the conquest of the Achaemenid Empire by Alexander the Great.

Persian art.fact: The rock reliefs of the preceding Persian Selucids and Parthians are generally smaller and more crude, and not all direct royal commissions as the Sasanian ones clearly were.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India

Persian art.fact: At Behistun an earlier relief including a lion was adapted into a reclining Herakles in a fully Hellenistic style; he reclines on a lion skin.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Other reliefs in Iran include the _____ king in shallow relief at Shikaft-e Gulgul; not all sites with Persian reliefs are in modern Iran
Persian art.fact: Other reliefs in Iran include the Assyrian king in shallow relief at Shikaft-e Gulgul; not all sites with Persian reliefs are in modern Iran. The standard catalogue of pre-Islamic Persian reliefs lists the known examples (as at 1984) as follows: Lullubi #1–4; Elam #5–19; Assyrian #20–21; Achaemenid #22–30; Late/Post-Achaemenid and Seleucid #31–35; Parthian #36–49; Sasanian #50–84; others #85–88.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: The Parthian Empire existed from 247 BC to 224 AD in what is now _____ and several territories outside it
Persian art.fact: The Parthian Empire existed from 247 BC to 224 AD in what is now Greater Iran and several territories outside it.

Persian art.question: Even after the period of the _____ dynasty, art in its style continued in surrounding areas for some time
Persian art.fact: The Parthian Empire existed from 247 BC to 224 AD in what is now Greater Iran and several territories outside it. Parthian places are often overlooked in excavations, and Parthian layers difficult to distinguish from those around them.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Even in narrative representations, figures look frontally out to the viewer rather than at each other, a feature that anticipates the art of _____, medieval Europe and Byzantium
Persian art.fact: Even in narrative representations, figures look frontally out to the viewer rather than at each other, a feature that anticipates the art of Late Antiquity, medieval Europe and Byzantium.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India

Persian art.fact: The excavations at Dura-Europos in the 20th century provided many new discoveries. The classical archaeologist and director of the excavations, Michael Rostovtzeff, realized that the art of the first centuries AD, Palmyra, Dura Europos, but also in Iran up to the Buddhist India followed the same principles.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: He called this artwork _____ art
Persian art.fact: He called this artwork Parthian art. The most characteristic feature of the "Parthian" art is frontality which is not a special feature of Iranic or Parthian art and first appeared in the art of Palmyra.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India

Persian art.fact: He called this artwork Parthian art. The most characteristic feature of the "Parthian" art is frontality which is not a special feature of Iranic or Parthian art and first appeared in the art of Palmyra.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: This art is better thought of as a local development common to the middle _____ region
Persian art.fact: There are doubts whether this art can be called a "Parthian" art or that it should be associated with any particular regional area; there is no evidence that this art was created outside the middle-Euphrates region then brought to Palmyra for example. This art is better thought of as a local development common to the middle Euphrates region.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Parthian rhyta continued the _____ style, but in the best the animals at the terminal (or protome) are more naturalistic, probably under Greek influence
Persian art.fact: Parthian rhyta continued the Achaemenid style, but in the best the animals at the terminal (or protome) are more naturalistic, probably under Greek influence. It began a new era in Iran and Mesopotamia, which in many ways was built on Achaemenid traditions, including the art of the period.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India

Persian art.fact: At times the Levant, much of Anatolia and parts of Egypt and Arabia were under its control.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India

Persian art.fact: It began a new era in Iran and Mesopotamia, which in many ways was built on Achaemenid traditions, including the art of the period.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India

Persian art.fact: Nevertheless, there were also other influences on art of the period that came from as far as China and the Mediterranean.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: The surviving art of the _____ is best seen in its architecture, reliefs and metalwork, and there are some surviving paintings from what was evidently a widespread production
Persian art.fact: The surviving art of the Sasanians is best seen in its architecture, reliefs and metalwork, and there are some surviving paintings from what was evidently a widespread production.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Free standing sculptures faded out of popularity in this time as compared to the period under the Parthians, but the _____ of Shapur I (r
Persian art.fact: Free standing sculptures faded out of popularity in this time as compared to the period under the Parthians, but the Colossal Statue of Shapur I (r. AD 240–272) is a major exception, carved from a stalagmite grown in a cave; there are literary mentions of other colossal statues of kings, now lost.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: The important _____ rock reliefs are covered above, and the Parthian tradition of moulded stucco decoration to buildings continued, also including large figurative scenes
Persian art.fact: The important Sasanian rock reliefs are covered above, and the Parthian tradition of moulded stucco decoration to buildings continued, also including large figurative scenes. Persian art.subject: Ancient India

Persian art.fact: The important Sasanian rock reliefs are covered above, and the Parthian tradition of moulded stucco decoration to buildings continued, also including large figurative scenes. Surviving Sasanian art depicts courtly and chivalric scenes, with considerable grandeur of style, reflecting the lavish life and display of the Sasanian court as recorded by Byzantine ambassadors.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Representations are often arranged like a coat of arms, which in turn may have had a strong influence on the production of art in Europe and _____
Persian art.fact: Representations are often arranged like a coat of arms, which in turn may have had a strong influence on the production of art in Europe and East Asia.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Although Parthian art preferred the front view, the narrative representations of the _____ art often features figures shown in the profile or a three-quarter view
Persian art.fact: Although Parthian art preferred the front view, the narrative representations of the Sassanian art often features figures shown in the profile or a three-quarter view.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: One of the few sites where wall-paintings survived in quantity is _____ in modern Tajikistan, and ancient Sogdia, which was barely, if at all, under the control of the central Sasanian power
Persian art.fact: One of the few sites where wall-paintings survived in quantity is Panjakent in modern Tajikistan, and ancient Sogdia, which was barely, if at all, under the control of the central Sasanian power.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: The old city was abandoned in the decades after the _____ eventually took the city in 722 and has been extensively excavated in modern times
Persian art.fact: The old city was abandoned in the decades after the Muslims eventually took the city in 722 and has been extensively excavated in modern times.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Large areas of wall paintings survived from the palace and private houses, which are mostly now in the _____ or Tashkent
Persian art.fact: Large areas of wall paintings survived from the palace and private houses, which are mostly now in the Hermitage Museum or Tashkent.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: At Bishapur floor mosaics in a broadly _____-Roman style have survived, and these were probably widespread in other elite settings, perhaps made by craftsmen from the Greek world
Persian art.fact: At Bishapur floor mosaics in a broadly Greco-Roman style have survived, and these were probably widespread in other elite settings, perhaps made by craftsmen from the Greek world.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: A number of _____ silver vessels have survived, especially rather large plates or bowls used to serve food
Persian art.fact: A number of Sasanid silver vessels have survived, especially rather large plates or bowls used to serve food.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: These were exported to _____, and also westwards
Persian art.fact: These were exported to China, and also westwards. In simpler forms it seems to have been available to a wide range of the population, and was a popular luxury export to Byzantium and China, even appearing in elite burials from the period in Japan.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Sasanian glass continued and developed _____ glass technology
Persian art.fact: Sasanian glass continued and developed Roman glass technology.

Persian art.fact: In simpler forms it seems to have been available to a wide range of the population, and was a popular luxury export to Byzantium and China, even appearing in elite burials from the period in Japan.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India

Persian art.fact: Carpets evidently could reach a high level of sophistication, as the praise lavished on the lost royal Baharestan Carpet by the Muslim conquerors shows.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: The Sogdians were especially talented in metalworking, and their work in this field inspired the _____, who were among their patrons together with the Turks
Persian art.fact: This influence on the Chinese ranged from metallurgy to music. The Sogdians were especially talented in metalworking, and their work in this field inspired the Chinese, who were among their patrons together with the Turks.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Today, the _____ are best known for their paintings, but they had a distinctive sculpture and architecture as well
Persian art.fact: Today, the Sogdians are best known for their paintings, but they had a distinctive sculpture and architecture as well. The Sogdians were especially talented in metalworking, and their work in this field inspired the Chinese, who were among their patrons together with the Turks.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: The Sogdian metalwork may be confused with _____ metalwork, and the two are still confused by some scholars today
Persian art.fact: The Sogdian metalwork may be confused with Sasanian metalwork, and the two are still confused by some scholars today. Thanks to the work of archaeologist Boris Marshak, several characteristic of Sogdian metalwork have been established: with respect to Sasanian vessels, Sogdian productions are less massive, their shape differs from the Sasanian, as do the techniques employed in their production.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Further, the designs of _____ productions are more dynamic
Persian art.fact: The Sogdian metalwork may be confused with Sasanian metalwork, and the two are still confused by some scholars today. Thanks to the work of archaeologist Boris Marshak, several characteristic of Sogdian metalwork have been established: with respect to Sasanian vessels, Sogdian productions are less massive, their shape differs from the Sasanian, as do the techniques employed in their production.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: These places were decorated with remarkable paintings, an art in which the _____ excelled
Persian art.fact: The Sogdians lived in architecturally complex abodes that resembled their temples. These places were decorated with remarkable paintings, an art in which the Sogdians excelled.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: They also depict stories and epics drawing on Iranian, _____ (Manichaean, Nestorian) and Indian themes
Persian art.fact: They also depict stories and epics drawing on Iranian, Near Eastern (Manichaean, Nestorian) and Indian themes.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Sogdian religious art reflects the religious affiliations of the _____, and this knowledge is derived mostly from paintings and ossuaries
Persian art.fact: Sogdian religious art reflects the religious affiliations of the Sogdians, and this knowledge is derived mostly from paintings and ossuaries. The Sogdians were storytellers: they loved to recount stories.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: In these paintings we see how the Sogdians saw themselves." _____ paintings were destroyed during the several invasions they suffered in their land
Persian art.fact: In these paintings we see how the Sogdians saw themselves." Many Sogdian paintings were destroyed during the several invasions they suffered in their land.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Of the works which survived, some of the best known are the _____ murals and the Penjikent murals
Persian art.fact: Of the works which survived, some of the best known are the Afrasiab murals and the Penjikent murals.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Turkic peoples became increasingly important in _____, especially the eastern parts, leading to a cultural Turko-Persian tradition
Persian art.fact: Turkic peoples became increasingly important in Greater Iran, especially the eastern parts, leading to a cultural Turko-Persian tradition.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Nishapur during the _____, especially the 9th and 10th centuries, was one of the great centres of pottery and related arts
Persian art.fact: Nishapur during the Islamic Golden Age, especially the 9th and 10th centuries, was one of the great centres of pottery and related arts.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Most of the ceramic artefacts discovered in _____ are preserved in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City, and museums in Tehran and Mashhad
Persian art.fact: Nishapur during the Islamic Golden Age, especially the 9th and 10th centuries, was one of the great centres of pottery and related arts. Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Ceramics produced at _____ showed links with Sasanian art and Central Asian art
Persian art.fact: Nishapur during the Islamic Golden Age, especially the 9th and 10th centuries, was one of the great centres of pottery and related arts. Most of the ceramic artefacts discovered in Nishapur are preserved in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City, and museums in Tehran and Mashhad.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India

Persian art.fact: Gold and silver equivalents apparently existed but have been mostly recycled for their precious materials; the few survivals were mostly traded north for furs and then buried as grave goods in Siberia.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: The rich silk textiles that were an important export from _____ also continued to use the animal, and sometimes human, figures of their Sasanid predecessors
Persian art.fact: The rich silk textiles that were an important export from Persia also continued to use the animal, and sometimes human, figures of their Sasanid predecessors.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: These pieces were typically earthenware vessels with black slip lettering in _____ script painted on a base of white slip
Persian art.fact: These pieces were typically earthenware vessels with black slip lettering in Kufi script painted on a base of white slip.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Samarqand and _____ were both centres of production for this kind of pottery
Persian art.fact: Samarqand and Nishapur were both centres of production for this kind of pottery. During their time, the center of culture, politics and art production shifted from Damascus and Baghdad to Merv, Nishapur, Rayy, and Isfahan, all in Iran.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: During their time, the center of culture, politics and art production shifted from _____ and Baghdad to Merv, Nishapur, Rayy, and Isfahan, all in Iran
Persian art.fact: During their time, the center of culture, politics and art production shifted from Damascus and Baghdad to Merv, Nishapur, Rayy, and Isfahan, all in Iran.

Persian art.question: Seljuq palace centres often featured _____ stucco figures
Persian art.fact: Seljuq palace centres often featured Seljuk stucco figures.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Because of increased production, many relics have survived from the _____ era and can be easily dated
Persian art.fact: Because of increased production, many relics have survived from the Seljuk era and can be easily dated. It is, therefore, easy to mistake Seljuk art as new developments rather than inheritance from classical Iranian and Turkic sources.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: It is, therefore, easy to mistake _____ art as new developments rather than inheritance from classical Iranian and Turkic sources
Persian art.fact: Because of increased production, many relics have survived from the Seljuk era and can be easily dated. It is, therefore, easy to mistake Seljuk art as new developments rather than inheritance from classical Iranian and Turkic sources.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: This is the earliest pottery anywhere to use overglaze enamel painting, which only began in China slightly later, and in _____ in the 18th century
Persian art.fact: This is the earliest pottery anywhere to use overglaze enamel painting, which only began in China slightly later, and in Europe in the 18th century.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Across the _____ era, from Iran to Iraq, a unification of book painting can be seen
Persian art.fact: Across the Seljuk era, from Iran to Iraq, a unification of book painting can be seen.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: The Persians gradually adopted _____ scripts after the conquest, and Persian calligraphy became an important artistic medium, often used as part of the decoration of other works in most media
Persian art.fact: The Persians gradually adopted Arabic scripts after the conquest, and Persian calligraphy became an important artistic medium, often used as part of the decoration of other works in most media.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: A rich civilization developed under these "little khans," who were originally subservient to the _____ emperor, but rapidly became independent
Persian art.fact: After his death, his empire was divided among his sons, forming many dynasties: the Yuan in China, the Ilkhanids in Iran and the Golden Horde in northern Iran and southern Russia, the latter two converting to Islam within a few decades. A rich civilization developed under these "little khans," who were originally subservient to the Yuan emperor, but rapidly became independent.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Architectural activity intensified as the _____ became sedentary, and retained traces of their nomadic origins, such as the north–south orientation of the buildings
Persian art.fact: Architectural activity intensified as the Mongols became sedentary, and retained traces of their nomadic origins, such as the north–south orientation of the buildings.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: At the same time a process of "iranisation" took place, and construction according to previously established types, such as the "_____ plan" mosques, was resumed
Persian art.fact: At the same time a process of "iranisation" took place, and construction according to previously set up types, such as the "Iranian plan" mosques, was resumed.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: New techniques in ceramics appeared, such as the lajvardina (a variation on lusterware), and _____ influence is perceptible in all arts
Persian art.fact: New techniques in ceramics appeared, such as the lajvardina (a variation on lusterware), and Chinese influence is perceptible in all arts.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: From the start paper was used, rather than parchment as in _____
Persian art.fact: From the start paper was used, rather than parchment as in Europe.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Yet their simple control of the world at that time, particularly in the 13–15th centuries, reflected itself in the idealised appearance of _____ as Mongols
Persian art.fact: These same Mongols intermarried with the Persians and Turks of Central Asia, even adopting their religion and languages. Yet their simple control of the world at that time, particularly in the 13–15th centuries, reflected itself in the idealised appearance of Persians as Mongols.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Though the ethnic make-up gradually blended into the _____ and Mesopotamian local populations, the Mongol stylism continued well after, and crossed into Asia Minor and even North Africa
Persian art.fact: Though the ethnic make-up gradually blended into the Iranian and Mesopotamian local populations, the Mongol stylism continued well after, and crossed into Asia Minor and even North Africa.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Within the group of _____ rugs produced by the countries of the so-called "rug belt", the Persian carpet stands out by the variety and elaborateness of its designs
Persian art.fact: Within the group of Oriental rugs produced by the countries of the so-called "rug belt", the Persian carpet stands out by the variety and elaborateness of its designs.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: This article covers the art of _____ up to 1925, and the end of the Qajar dynasty; for later art see Iranian modern and contemporary art, and for traditional crafts see arts of Iran
Persian art.fact: Persian art or Iranian art (Persian: هنر ایرانی, romanized: Honar-è Irâni) has one of the richest art heritages in world history and has been strong in many media including architecture, painting, weaving, pottery, calligraphy, metalworking and sculpture. At different times, influences from the art of neighbouring civilizations have been very important, and latterly Persian art gave and received major influences as part of the wider styles of Islamic art.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Shortly after Susa was first settled _____ years ago, its inhabitants erected a temple on a monumental platform that rose over the flat surrounding landscape
Persian art.fact: Shortly after Susa was first settled 6000 years ago, its inhabitants erected a temple on a monumental platform that rose over the flat surrounding landscape.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Sassanian reliefs are concentrated in the first _____ years of the dynasty, though one important set are 6th-century, and at relatively few sites, mostly in the Sasanian heartland
Persian art.fact: Sassanian reliefs are concentrated in the first 80 years of the dynasty, though one important set are 6th-century, and at relatively few sites, mostly in the Sasanian heartland.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: As such, they represent different, simultaneous lines of tradition, and reflect the history of _____ and its various peoples
Persian art.fact: Though the ethnic make-up gradually blended into the Iranian and Mesopotamian local populations, the Mongol stylism continued well after, and crossed into Asia Minor and even North Africa. As such, they represent different, simultaneous lines of tradition, and reflect the history of Iran and its various peoples.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Their patterns and designs have set an artistic tradition for court manufactories which was kept alive during the entire duration of the _____ up to the last royal dynasty of Iran
Persian art.fact: Their patterns and designs have set an artistic tradition for court manufactories which was kept alive during the entire duration of the Persian Empire up to the last royal dynasty of Iran.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Exceptional individual _____ carpets include the Ardabil Carpet (now in London and Los Angeles) and the Coronation Carpet (now in Copenhagen)
Persian art.fact: The carpets woven in the Safavid court manufactories of Isfahan during the sixteenth century are famous for their elaborate colours and artistical design, and are treasured in museums and private collections all over the world today. Exceptional individual Safavid carpets include the Ardabil Carpet (now in London and Los Angeles) and the Coronation Carpet (now in Copenhagen).

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Much earlier, the _____ is a lost Sasanian carpet for the royal palace at Ctesiphon, and the oldest significant carpet, the Pazyryk Carpet was possibly made in Persia
Persian art.fact: Much earlier, the Baharestan Carpet is a lost Sasanian carpet for the royal palace at Ctesiphon, and the oldest significant carpet, the Pazyryk Carpet was possibly made in Persia.

Persian art.subject: Ancient India
Persian art.question: Town manufactories like those of _____ have played an important historical role in reviving the tradition of carpet weaving after periods of decline
